knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Divergence Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order linearization-error representation of Bregman divergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h\) be a proper convex function differentiable on an open convex set \(U\) in a finite-dimensional real vector space. For \(x,y\in U\), the Bregman divergence generated by \(h\) is \[D_h(x,y):=h(x)-h(y)-\langle\nabla h(y),x-y\rangle.\] Convexity gives \(D_h(x,y)\ge0\), and strict convexity gives \(D_h(x,y)=0\) only when \(x=y\). In general, \(D_h\) need not be symmetric and need not satisfy the triangle inequality, so it is a divergence rather than a metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bregman divergence is the gap between a convex function and its first-order affine approximation at the base point.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is open and convex in a finite-dimensional real vector space.
\(h\) is proper, convex, and differentiable on \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_h(x,y)=h(x)-h(y)-\langle\nabla h(y),x-y\rangle\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Bregman divergence from base point y to evaluation point x

knowledge_statements.title: Euclidean Quadratic Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic mirror geometry induced by a positive-definite linear metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite, and define \(\phi(x)=\tfrac12 x^{\mathsf T}Hx\). Then \(\nabla\phi(x)=Hx\), \(\phi^*(y)=\tfrac12y^{\mathsf T}H^{-1}y\), and \[D_\phi(u,v)=\tfrac12(u-v)^{\mathsf T}H(u-v)=\tfrac12\|u-v\|_H^2.\] Consequently, the Bregman projection of \(v\) onto a nonempty closed convex set \(C\) is the metric projection \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in C}\|u-v\|_H^2\). For \(H=I\), this reduces to ordinary squared Euclidean distance and Euclidean projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite quadratic mirror map produces squared metric distance; its Bregman projection is exactly projection in that metric.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex when projection is invoked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_\phi(u,v)=\tfrac12\|u-v\|_H^2\), and Bregman projection equals \(H\)-metric projection.

knowledge_statements.title: Entropy Geometry on the Simplex
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Negative-entropy Bregman geometry on the probability simplex interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Delta_n=\{x\in\mathbb{R}_+^n:\sum_i x_i=1\}\) and define \(\phi(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\log x_i\), with \(0\log0=0\). For \(v\in\operatorname{ri}(\Delta_n)\), \((\nabla\phi(v))_i=1+\log v_i\), and for \(u\in\Delta_n\), \[D_\phi(u,v)=\sum_{i=1}^n u_i\log\frac{u_i}{v_i},\] using \(0\log(0/v_i)=0\). The mirror-proximal update minimizing \(\eta\langle g,u\rangle+D_\phi(u,v)\) over \(\Delta_n\) is \[u_i^+=\frac{v_i e^{-\eta g_i}}{\sum_jv_j e^{-\eta g_j}}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative entropy generates Kullback–Leibler divergence on the simplex, and its linearized mirror step is the normalized multiplicative-weights update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_\phi(u,v)=\sum_i u_i\log(u_i/v_i)\), with the displayed multiplicative update.

knowledge_statements.title: Power-Type Mirror Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable power potential and its coordinatewise mirror map on Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(q>1\) and define \(\phi_q:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) by \(\phi_q(x)=q^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n|x_i|^q\). Then \[(\nabla\phi_q(x))_i=|x_i|^{q-2}x_i,\qquad \phi_q^*(y)=\frac{1}{q^*}\sum_{i=1}^n|y_i|^{q^*},\] where \(q^*=q/(q-1)\) and every expression \(|s|^{r-2}s\) is assigned its continuous value \(0\) at \(s=0\). The inverse mirror map is \((\nabla\phi_q^*(y))_i=|y_i|^{q^*-2}y_i\), and \[D_{\phi_q}(u,v)=\frac1q\sum_{i=1}^n\bigl(|u_i|^q-|v_i|^q-q|v_i|^{q-2}v_i(u_i-v_i)\bigr).\] Hence both the mirror map and its inverse act coordinatewise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The separable q-power potential has a coordinatewise power gradient, a conjugate-exponent inverse map, and an explicit separable Bregman divergence, with the coordinate maps continuously defined as zero at zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla\phi_q^*=(\nabla\phi_q)^{-1}\), with the displayed separable Bregman divergence.

knowledge_statements.title: p-Norm Mirror Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strongly convex squared-norm mirror potential for the regime \(1<p\leq2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(1<p\leq2\) and define \(\psi_p(x)=\|x\|_p^2/[2(p-1)]\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\). This function is \(1\)-strongly convex with respect to \(\|\cdot\|_p\). For \(x
eq0\), its mirror coordinate is \[(
abla\psi_p(x))_i= rac{\|x\|_p^{2-p}}{p-1}|x_i|^{p-2}x_i,\] with \(
abla\psi_p(0)=0\). Consequently, \[D_{\psi_p}(u,v)\geq rac12\|u-v\|_p^2.\] Its conjugate is \(\psi_p^*(y)=	frac{p-1}{2}\|y\|_{p^*}^2\), where \(p^*=p/(p-1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For 1<p≤2, a scaled squared p-norm is one-strongly convex and gives explicit primal and dual mirror coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Power–Norm Parameter Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter conditions separating differentiability, strong-convexity, and dual-exponent behavior of power geometries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the separable power potential \(\phi_q(x)=\|x\|_q^q/q\), the mirror map is single-valued and continuous on \(\mathbb{R}^n\) exactly in the differentiable regime \(q>1\), with conjugate exponent \(q^*=q/(q-1)\). For the squared-norm potential \(x\mapsto\|x\|_p^2/2\), the standard dimension-free strong-convexity estimate is \((p-1)\)-strong convexity relative to \(\|\cdot\|_p\) when \(1<p\leq2\); scaling by \(1/(p-1)\) makes the modulus one. At \(p=1\), differentiability and positive strong convexity fail, while for \(p>2\) this particular dimension-free quadratic lower bound is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Power mirrors require exponent above one; squared p-norm geometry has the standard dimension-free strong-convexity normalization only for 1<p≤2.
assumptions_latex: Strong convexity is measured relative to the stated \(p\)-norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q>1\) ensures differentiability, while \(1<p\leq2\) yields the stated dimension-free squared-norm strong-convexity regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Entropy Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Von Neumann entropy geometry on positive-definite density matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D_d=\{X\in\mathbb S_+^d:\operatorname{tr}X=1\}\) and define \(\Phi(X)=\operatorname{tr}(X\log X)\), with the continuous convention at zero. For \(Y\in\operatorname{ri}(\mathcal D_d)\), \(\nabla\Phi(Y)=\log Y+I\), and for \(X\in\mathcal D_d\), \[D_\Phi(X,Y)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(X(\log X-\log Y)\bigr).\] For a symmetric direction \(G\) and \(\eta>0\), the entropy mirror step over \(\mathcal D_d\) is \[X^+=\frac{\exp(\log Y-\eta G)}{\operatorname{tr}\exp(\log Y-\eta G)}.\] No commutativity between \(Y\) and \(G\) is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Von Neumann entropy generates quantum relative entropy, and its mirror step is a trace-normalized matrix exponential update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_\Phi(X,Y)=\operatorname{tr}(X(\log X-\log Y))\), with the displayed matrix-exponential update.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formulas are plausible and standard, but no citation is supplied for the matrix-entropy gradient, boundary convention, quantum relative entropy, or noncommutative exponential update.

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Three-Point Principle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact three-point identity for a differentiable convex generator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\) be an open convex subset of a finite-dimensional real vector space, and let \(\phi:U	o\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable and convex. For all \(x,y,z\in U\), \[D_\phi(z,x)-D_\phi(z,y)-D_\phi(y,x)=\langle
abla\phi(y)-
abla\phi(x),z-yangle.\] Equivalently, \[\langle
abla\phi(y)-
abla\phi(x),y-zangle=D_\phi(z,y)+D_\phi(y,x)-D_\phi(z,x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The difference of three Bregman divergences equals a gradient-difference pairing; reversing the pairing reverses the sign of the divergence difference.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_\phi(z,x)-D_\phi(z,y)-D_\phi(y,x)=\langle\nabla\phi(y)-\nabla\phi(x),z-y\rangle\).

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Pythagorean Principle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bregman projection inequality for a convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be an open convex subset of a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(C\subseteq U\) be nonempty and convex, and let \(\phi:U\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable and strictly convex. Fix \(x\in U\), and suppose \[y\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in C}D_\phi(u,x).\] Then \[\langle\nabla\phi(y)-\nabla\phi(x),z-y\rangle\geq0\qquad\text{for every }\(z\in C\).\] Consequently, \[D_\phi(z,x)\geq D_\phi(z,y)+D_\phi(y,x)\qquad\text{for every }\(z\in C\).\] Equality holds for any \(z\in C\) for which the displayed optimality pairing is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Bregman projection splits the divergence from any feasible comparison point into two divergence legs plus a nonnegative optimality residual.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in U\), and the displayed Bregman projection \(y\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_\phi(z,x)\geq D_\phi(z,y)+D_\phi(y,x)\) for every \(z\in C\).

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Proximal Comparison Principle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step comparison inequality for a composite Bregman proximal update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(U\subseteq X\) be open and convex, and let \(C\subseteq U\) be convex. Let \(h:C\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex, and let \(\phi:U\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable and strictly convex. For \(x\in C\), \(g\in X^*\), and \(\eta>0\), suppose \[x^+\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in C}\left\{\eta\langle g,u\rangle+\eta h(u)+D_\phi(u,x)\right\}.\] Then every \(z\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}h\) satisfies \[\eta\bigl(\langle g,x^+-z\rangle+h(x^+)-h(z)\bigr)\leq D_\phi(z,x)-D_\phi(z,x^+)-D_\phi(x^+,x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite Bregman proximal step bounds its linearized composite-objective gap by the decrease in comparison divergence minus the divergence of the step.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite-dimensional, \(U\subseteq X\) is open and convex, and \(C\subseteq U\) is convex.
\(x\in C\), \(g\in X^*\), \(\eta>0\), and the displayed minimizer exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta(\langle g,x^+-z\rangle+h(x^+)-h(z))\leq D_\phi(z,x)-D_\phi(z,x^+)-D_\phi(x^+,x)\) for every \(z\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}h\).

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Telescoping Principle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Summation rule converting one-step Bregman comparisons into endpoint and residual terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a positive integer, let \(U\) be an open convex subset of a finite-dimensional real vector space, and let \(\phi:U\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable and convex. Let \(x_1,\ldots,x_{T+1},z\in U\), and suppose \(a_1,\ldots,a_T\in\mathbb{R}\) satisfy \[a_t\leq D_\phi(z,x_t)-D_\phi(z,x_{t+1})-D_\phi(x_{t+1},x_t),\qquad t=1,\ldots,T.\] Then \[\sum_{t=1}^T a_t\leq D_\phi(z,x_1)-D_\phi(z,x_{T+1})-\sum_{t=1}^T D_\phi(x_{t+1},x_t).\] Since \(D_\phi\) is nonnegative, \[\sum_{t=1}^T a_t\leq D_\phi(z,x_1).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summing the one-step Bregman comparisons cancels consecutive comparison divergences, leaving the initial-minus-final divergence and the cumulative nonnegative movement term.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is open and convex, and \(\phi:U\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable and convex.
The displayed one-step inequalities hold for \(t=1,\ldots,T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{t=1}^T a_t\leq D_\phi(z,x_1)-D_\phi(z,x_{T+1})-\sum_{t=1}^T D_\phi(x_{t+1},x_t)\leq D_\phi(z,x_1)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Mirror Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration-dependent Bregman geometry with uniform curvature control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a convex subset of a finite-dimensional vector space. A variable-metric mirror geometry is a sequence \((h_t,\|\cdot\|_t)_{t\ge1}\) such that each \(h_t:C\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable on the step domain and \(\mu_t\)-strongly convex with respect to \(\|\cdot\|_t\), meaning \(D_{h_t}(x,y)\ge \tfrac{\mu_t}{2}\|x-y\|_t^2\) for all admissible \(x,y\in C\). For uniform stability one additionally requires \(\inf_t\mu_t>0\); convergence analyses may also impose controlled inter-iteration variation of \(D_{h_t}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable-metric mirror geometry uses a changing mirror map and norm, with each Bregman divergence uniformly controlling displacement and often with bounded variation across iterations.
assumptions_latex: Each \(h_t\) is differentiable on the domain where its Bregman divergence is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_{h_t}(x,y)\ge \tfrac{\mu_t}{2}\|x-y\|_t^2\) for every admissible \(x,y\in C\).

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Geometry Ownership Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predictability boundary for stochastic mirror-descent geometry selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_t\) satisfy \(\mathbb E[g_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\in\partial f(x_t)\). Standard stochastic mirror-descent conditioning applies when the selected geometry \(h_t\) and step size \(\eta_t\) are \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable. If \(h_t\) is instead chosen using the same realized \(g_t\) before forming the update, then the geometry-dependent iterate and divergence are generally correlated with the oracle noise; the conditional cancellation used in the usual analysis need not hold. Such a rule requires a separate coupled analysis, sample splitting, or an enlarged algorithmic model and cannot automatically inherit predictable-geometry guarantees.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Mirror Descent Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mirror-descent update driven by a conditionally unbiased stochastic first-order oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(h\) be differentiable and strongly convex, and initialize \(x_1\in C\). With filtration \((\mathcal F_t)\), at iteration \(t\) obtain an oracle output \(G_t\) satisfying \(\mathbb E[G_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\in\partial f(x_t)\) and a stated conditional moment bound. For a predictable step size \(\eta_t>0\), set \(x_{t+1}\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{x\in C}\{\eta_t\langle G_t,x\rangle+D_h(x,x_t)\}\). After \(T\) calls, output the declared last iterate or the weighted average \(\bar x_T=(\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_tx_t)/(\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stochastic mirror descent replaces the exact subgradient by a conditionally unbiased oracle sample, uses predictable step sizes, and returns a declared last or averaged iterate.
assumptions_latex: The required conditional dual-norm moment of \(G_t\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{t+1}\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{x\in C}\{\eta_t\langle G_t,x\rangle+D_h(x,x_t)\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Online Mirror Descent Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adversarial online convex optimization with a fixed Bregman geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a nonempty closed convex subset of a finite-dimensional normed space, and let \(h:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable and strongly convex. Initialize \(x_1\in X\). At round \(t\), play \(x_t\), observe a convex loss \(f_t:X\to\mathbb{R}\) and a subgradient \(g_t\in\partial f_t(x_t)\), choose \(\eta_t>0\), and update
\[
x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{\eta_t\langle g_t,x\rangle+D_h(x,x_t)\right\}.
\]
After \(T\) rounds, output the played sequence or the weighted average \(\bar x_T=(\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t)^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t x_t\); online performance is measured by regret \(\sum_{t=1}^T(f_t(x_t)-f_t(u))\) against \(u\in X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each round, online mirror descent linearizes the revealed loss and takes a Bregman-proximal step; its interface returns iterates or an average and is evaluated by regret.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is differentiable and strongly convex on \(X\).
Each revealed \(f_t\) is convex and admits \(g_t\in\partial f_t(x_t)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{t+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\{\eta_t\langle g_t,x\rangle+D_h(x,x_t)\}\).

notation.meaning: observed loss subgradient at the played point

knowledge_statements.title: Mirror-Prox Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates one-step mirror descent from extragradient methods for monotone variational inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be closed and convex, let \(h\) generate the Bregman divergence \(D_h\), and let \(F:X\to X^*\) be monotone. Mirror-Prox uses two oracle evaluations:
\[
y_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{\eta_t\langle F(x_t),x\rangle+D_h(x,x_t)\},\qquad
x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{\eta_t\langle F(y_t),x\rangle+D_h(x,x_t)\}.
\]
Thus it lies outside ordinary one-evaluation mirror descent. The distinction is substantive for general monotone problems: replacing \(F(y_t)\) by \(F(x_t)\) removes the predictive correction used to control the operator variation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mirror-Prox makes a predictive Bregman step and then a corrected step using a second operator evaluation, placing it beyond ordinary one-evaluation mirror descent.
assumptions_latex: \(D_h\) is well-defined for the displayed prox subproblems.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is evaluated at both \(x_t\) and \(y_t\), so the update is not an ordinary single-evaluation mirror-descent step.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-evaluation update correctly describes the Mirror-Prox boundary, but no inspectable source with a section, theorem, or page locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Accelerated Mirror-Method Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Marks the additional structure required for acceleration beyond nonsmooth mirror descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For minimizing a general Lipschitz convex function using only a local first-order oracle, changing Euclidean projection to a Bregman prox does not by itself yield an accelerated accuracy order. Accelerated mirror-type schemes require additional structure, such as a differentiable objective with Lipschitz gradient, a relatively smooth model, or another oracle model supporting controlled upper approximations and estimate-sequence coupling. Consequently, the update
\[
x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{\eta_t\langle g_t,x\rangle+D_h(x,x_t)\}
\]
with arbitrary nonsmooth subgradients \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\) remains in the nonsmooth mirror-descent regime unless such extra structure is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bregman geometry alone does not accelerate general nonsmooth subgradient optimization; acceleration needs smoothness, relative smoothness, or a stronger model-oracle structure.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and accessed only through local first-order information.
No smoothness or stronger model-oracle assumption is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed Bregman subgradient update cannot be classified as an accelerated mirror method solely from its choice of geometry.

notation.meaning: Bregman divergence defining the prox geometry

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The boundary claim invokes oracle-complexity and acceleration distinctions across several frameworks; these require an authoritative lower-bound or acceleration source.

knowledge_statements.title: Classical Dual Averaging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unweighted dual averaging with one fixed prox function and increasing regularization scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(h:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be strongly convex with a tractable prox subproblem, and choose \(x_1\in\operatorname{dom}h\cap X\). For \(t=1,2,\ldots\), obtain \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\), form the cumulative dual vector \(s_t=\sum_{i=1}^t g_i\), choose \(\beta_t>0\), and set
\[
x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{\langle s_t,x\rangle+\beta_t h(x)\right\}.
\]
Stop according to a prescribed iteration or oracle budget and return the last iterate or a declared average of \(x_1,\ldots,x_T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical dual averaging accumulates all past subgradients in dual space and maps their sum back to the feasible set through a scaled strongly convex prox function.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is strongly convex and the prox subproblem has a minimizer.
\(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\) is available at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{t+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\{\langle\sum_{i=1}^t g_i,x\rangle+\beta_t h(x)\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Dual Averaging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual averaging with explicit nonnegative weights on past first-order information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(h\) be strongly convex on \(X\), and choose \(x_1\in X\). Given weights \(a_t>0\), at iteration \(t\) obtain \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\), update \(s_t=s_{t-1}+a_tg_t\) from \(s_0=0\), choose \(\beta_t>0\), and compute
\[
x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{\langle s_t,x\rangle+\beta_t h(x)\}.
\]
For \(A_T=\sum_{t=1}^T a_t\), the associated primal output is ordinarily \(\bar x_T=A_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T a_tx_t\), unless the last iterate is explicitly selected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted dual averaging accumulates weighted subgradients, applies a scaled prox map, and naturally reports the primal iterate average using the same weights.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is strongly convex and each displayed minimizer exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_t=\sum_{i=1}^t a_i g_i\) and \(x_{t+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\{\langle s_t,x\rangle+\beta_t h(x)\}\).

notation.meaning: weight of the current oracle vector

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Dual Averaging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual averaging with cumulative, possibly time-varying convex regularizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. Initialize \(s_0=0\). At iteration \(t\), obtain a first-order vector \(g_t\), choose a convex regularizer \(r_t:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), set \(s_t=s_{t-1}+g_t\), and update
\[
x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{\langle s_t,x\rangle+\sum_{i=0}^t r_i(x)\right\}.
\]
The cumulative regularizer must make the objective proper and attain a unique minimizer, for example by being strongly convex. A stopping rule fixes \(T\), after which the declared last iterate or primal average is returned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularized dual averaging minimizes the accumulated linearized losses plus all regularizers introduced so far, allowing the prox geometry and strength to vary over time.
assumptions_latex: Each \(r_t\) is proper and convex on \(X\).
\(\sum_{i=0}^t r_i\) makes every update objective coercive or otherwise uniquely minimized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{t+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\{\langle\sum_{i=1}^t g_i,x\rangle+\sum_{i=0}^t r_i(x)\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied for this cumulative-regularizer convention, whose indexing and relationship to regularized dual averaging vary across references.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite Dual Averaging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual averaging for an objective split into an oracle term and a proximable convex term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimizing \(F(x)=f(x)+\psi(x)\) over a nonempty closed convex set \(X\), where subgradients of \(f\) are queried and \(\psi\) is retained exactly. Let \(h\) be strongly convex, choose positive weights \(a_t\), define \(A_t=\sum_{i=1}^t a_i\), and accumulate \(s_t=\sum_{i=1}^t a_i g_i\) with \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\). Given \(\beta_t>0\), update
\[
x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{\langle s_t,x\rangle+A_t\psi(x)+\beta_t h(x)\}.
\]
After the stopping index \(T\), return a declared last iterate or weighted primal average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composite dual averaging linearizes only the oracle-accessed term while retaining the proximable convex term exactly with its cumulative weight in every prox subproblem.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(\psi\) are proper convex functions on \(X\).
\(a_t>0\), \(\beta_t>0\), and every update has a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{t+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\{\langle\sum_{i=1}^t a_i g_i,x\rangle+A_t\psi(x)+\beta_t h(x)\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Dual Averaging Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual averaging driven by conditionally unbiased stochastic first-order estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\mathcal F_t)\) be the history filtration and let \(F(x)=\mathbb E[f(x,\xi)]\) be convex on a closed convex set \(X\). Initialize \(s_0=0\) and \(x_1\in X\). At iteration \(t\), sample \(\xi_t\), obtain \(G_t=G(x_t,\xi_t)\) satisfying \(\mathbb E[G_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\in\partial F(x_t)\), update \(s_t=s_{t-1}+a_tG_t\), and set
\[
x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{\langle s_t,x\rangle+\beta_t h(x)\}.
\]
For a fixed budget \(T\), return \(\bar x_T=(\sum_{t=1}^T a_t)^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T a_tx_t\) or a declared last iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The stochastic interface replaces exact subgradients by conditionally unbiased estimates, accumulates them with weights, performs the usual dual-averaging prox map, and returns an iterate or average.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(h\) is strongly convex.
\(a_t>0\), \(\beta_t>0\), and the prox subproblem is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_t=\sum_{i=1}^t a_iG_i\) and \(x_{t+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\{\langle s_t,x\rangle+\beta_t h(x)\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Averaging Constructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted feasible averages associated with dual-averaging oracle weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_1,\ldots,x_T\in X\), where \(X\) is convex, and let \(a_t\ge 0\) with \(A_T=\sum_{t=1}^T a_t>0\). The primal average associated with these weights is
\[
\bar x_T=\frac{1}{A_T}\sum_{t=1}^T a_tx_t,
\]
which belongs to \(X\). If \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is convex, then
\[
f(\bar x_T)\leq \frac{1}{A_T}\sum_{t=1}^T a_tf(x_t).
\]
The recursive construction \(\bar x_t=(1-a_t/A_t)\bar x_{t-1}+(a_t/A_t)x_t\) is equivalent whenever \(A_{t-1}>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative dual-averaging weights define a feasible weighted primal average; convexity bounds its objective value by the correspondingly weighted average of iterate values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x_T\in X\) and \(f(\bar x_T)\leq A_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T a_tf(x_t)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Certificate Constructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A computable finite lower model paired with a feasible primal point to certify suboptimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a nonempty convex set and let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and convex with finite optimal value \(f^*=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\in\mathbb R\). Let \(x_t\in X\), \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\), and \(a_t\geq0\), where \(A_T=\sum_{t=1}^T a_t>0\). Define
\[
L_T(x)=\frac{1}{A_T}\sum_{t=1}^T a_t\bigl(f(x_t)+\langle g_t,x-x_t\rangle\bigr),
\qquad
\ell_T=\inf_{x\in X}L_T(x).
\]
Assume that \(\ell_T\in\mathbb R\) is computable. Convexity gives \(L_T(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), and hence \(\ell_T\leq f^*\). Therefore every \(\bar x_T\in X\) with \(f(\bar x_T)<+\infty\) satisfies
\[
0\leq f(\bar x_T)-f^*\leq f(\bar x_T)-\ell_T.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite weighted aggregate of supporting hyperplanes gives a computable global lower bound. Subtracting that bound from the finite objective value of a feasible primal point certifies an upper bound on its suboptimality.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty and convex, and \(f\) is proper and convex on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\leq f(\bar x_T)-f^*\leq f(\bar x_T)-\ell_T\).

notation.meaning: finite infimum of the aggregate lower model over X

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Primal–Dual Scaling Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility conditions for time-varying oracle weights, primal averages, and dual regularization scales.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A dynamic primal–dual scaling policy consists of weights \(a_t>0\), cumulative weights \(A_t=A_{t-1}+a_t\), and regularization scales \(\beta_t>0\). It is compatible with weighted dual averaging when the primal recursion and dual update use the same weights:
\[
\bar x_t=\frac{A_{t-1}}{A_t}\bar x_{t-1}+\frac{a_t}{A_t}x_t,
\qquad
s_t=s_{t-1}+a_tg_t,
\qquad
x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{\langle s_t,x\rangle+\beta_t h(x)\}.
\]
The policy is admissible only when every prox subproblem is attained; analyses may impose further monotonicity or growth conditions on \(\beta_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compatible scaling policy uses identical weights in primal averaging and dual accumulation, while positive regularization scales must keep every prox subproblem well posed.
assumptions_latex: Each scaled prox subproblem has a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal coefficient \(a_t/A_t\) matches the dual increment \(a_tg_t\), and the scaled dual update is well defined.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the asserted compatibility requirement that primal and dual weights must coincide; this is a framework-specific policy choice rather than a universal well-posedness condition.

knowledge_statements.title: Lazy Mirror Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mirror update obtained from the cumulative dual state rather than the latest primal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(h:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be strongly convex, choose \(s_0=0\), and fix positive weights \(a_t\) and scales \(\beta_t\). At iteration \(t\), query \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\), set \(s_t=s_{t-1}+a_tg_t\), and compute
\[
x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{\langle s_t,x\rangle+\beta_t h(x)\}.
\]
The method is lazy because the mirror map is applied to the accumulated dual state \(s_t\); unlike greedy mirror descent, its prox center is not explicitly the preceding primal iterate. Stop at a prescribed budget and return the declared last iterate or weighted average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lazy mirror descent accumulates gradients in dual space and only then applies the mirror map, making its update the dual-averaging form rather than a recentered greedy step.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is strongly convex and each update is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{t+1}\) is obtained from the cumulative dual state \(s_t=\sum_{i=1}^t a_i g_i\), not from an explicitly recentered divergence at \(x_t\).

knowledge_statements.title: Greedy Mirror Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Current-iterate, or greedy, mirror descent with a fixed Bregman geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space with dual \(E^*\) and pairing \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle\). Let \(C\subseteq E\) be nonempty, closed, and convex; let \(f:C\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be convex; and let \(h:U\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable and strictly convex on an open convex set \(U\supseteq C\). Initialize \(x_1\in C\). At iteration \(t\), obtain \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\subseteq E^*\), choose \(\eta_t>0\), and set \[x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\left\{\eta_t\langle g_t,x\rangle+D_h(x,x_t)\right\},\qquad D_h(x,y)=h(x)-h(y)-\langle\nabla h(y),x-y\rangle.\] Stop according to a prescribed iteration or accuracy rule and return either the last iterate or a specified weighted average of the iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Greedy mirror descent linearizes the objective at the current iterate and immediately performs a Bregman-proximal update from that iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space and \(C\subseteq E\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(f:C\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is convex and the required subgradients are available.
\(h:U\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable and strictly convex on an open convex set \(U\supseteq C\).
Each displayed minimization has a solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{t+1}\) is the current-iterate Bregman proximal response to \(g_t\).

notation.meaning: subgradient observed at the current iterate

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized-Leader Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-geometry correspondence between unconstrained greedy mirror descent and regularized cumulative linear optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose all iterates are interior and the mirror-descent optimality condition has no normal-cone term. With fixed differentiable strictly convex \(h\) and initialization \(x_1\), the update \(x_{t+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_x\{\eta_t\langle g_t,xangle+D_h(x,x_t)\}\) satisfies \(
abla h(x_{t+1})=
abla h(x_1)-\sum_{s=1}^t\eta_s g_s\). Consequently, \[x_{t+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{\left\langle\sum_{s=1}^t\eta_s g_s,xightangle+h(x)-\langle
abla h(x_1),xangleight\}.\] Thus the greedy iterates admit a regularized-leader representation with a fixed translated regularizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without active constraints, fixed-geometry mirror descent equals minimizing accumulated linear losses plus a translated mirror regularizer.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is differentiable and strictly convex, and the required minimizers are interior.
\(\eta_t>0\) and \(g_t\) belong to the dual space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{t+1}\) has both the greedy mirror-descent and fixed-regularizer cumulative-leader representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Time-Varying Regularization Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies why fixed-regularizer mirror-descent and regularized-leader equivalence fails under changing geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For time-dependent differentiable regularizers \(h_t\), the greedy update \(x_{t+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_x\{\eta_t\langle g_t,xangle+D_{h_t}(x,x_t)\}\) gives \[
abla h_t(x_{t+1})=
abla h_t(x_t)-\eta_t g_t.\] These identities do not telescope into a fixed-regularizer cumulative formula because generally \(
abla h_{t+1}(x_{t+1})
e
abla h_t(x_{t+1})\). Hence equivalence with ordinary regularized-leader updates requires either constant geometry or explicit correction terms accounting for \(
abla h_{t+1}(x_{t+1})-
abla h_t(x_{t+1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing the mirror regularizer destroys the dual-gradient telescoping behind the fixed-regularizer leader correspondence unless geometry-change corrections are included.
assumptions_latex: \(h_t\) is differentiable and strictly convex for every \(t\).
The updates are interior, so no normal-cone terms occur.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ordinary fixed-regularizer leader equivalence is not valid for arbitrary \((h_t)\) without correction terms.

children.title: Bregman Projection Methods
children.top_down_role: Projection constructions based on Bregman geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Set Bregman Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bregman projection of one point onto one convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a nonempty closed convex subset of a finite-dimensional space, and let \(h\) be differentiable and strictly convex on an open convex domain containing \(C\) and \(y\). The Bregman projection of \(y\) onto \(C\) is the possibly set-valued map \[P_C^h(y):=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}D_h(x,y),\qquad D_h(x,y)=h(x)-h(y)-\langle\nabla h(y),x-y\rangle.\] When the minimum is attained, strict convexity of \(h\) makes the projected point unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single-set Bregman projection minimizes the Bregman divergence from a reference point over one closed convex set.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is differentiable and strictly convex on the relevant domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_C^h(y)\) is a singleton consisting of the unique Bregman-nearest point in \(C\).

notation.meaning: Bregman projection onto C generated by h

children.title: Cyclic Bregman Projection
children.top_down_role: Projection families visiting constraint sets according to a recurring order.

knowledge_statements.title: Cyclic Bregman Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic cyclic projections onto finitely many convex constraint sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) be nonempty closed convex sets and let \(h\) generate well-defined single-set Bregman projections. Starting from \(x_0\) in the domain of \(h\), define \(i_k=1+(k\bmod m)\) and update \[x_{k+1}=P_{C_{i_k}}^h(x_k).\] One cycle consists of \(m\) consecutive updates, so every set is visited once per cycle. Stop under a prescribed residual or iteration rule and return the current iterate; convergence requires additional consistency and regularity hypotheses not included in this algorithm definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cyclic Bregman projection repeatedly projects onto each constraint set in a fixed periodic order.
assumptions_latex: Every required Bregman projection exists and is unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}\) is obtained by projecting \(x_k\) onto the next set in the fixed cycle.

notation.meaning: Bregman projection onto the ith constraint set
cyclic constraint index at iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cyclic update is a coherent algorithm and fits the leaf, but the record has no citation for this scheduled Bregman-projection convention.

children.title: Block Bregman Projection
children.top_down_role: Projection families acting on grouped constraints, coordinates, or product factors.

knowledge_statements.title: Block Bregman Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scheduled projection onto intersections of selected blocks of convex constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) be nonempty closed convex sets. At iteration \(k\), choose a nonempty block \(I_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), form \(C_{I_k}=\bigcap_{i\in I_k}C_i\), and update \[x_{k+1}=P_{C_{I_k}}^h(x_k).\] The block must have nonempty intersection and admit a well-defined Bregman projection. Stop under a prescribed residual or iteration rule and return the current iterate. Singleton blocks recover scheduled single-set projections, while the full block projects onto the entire intersection in one step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block Bregman projection projects each iterate onto the intersection of a scheduled subset of the constraint sets.
assumptions_latex: \(C_i\) is nonempty, closed, and convex for each \(i\).
Each scheduled block intersection \(C_{I_k}\) is nonempty.
Every required Bregman projection exists and is unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}\in C_{I_k}\) minimizes \(D_h(\cdot,x_k)\) over the selected block intersection.

notation.meaning: constraint block selected at iteration k
intersection of constraints in the selected block
Bregman projection onto the block intersection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source establishes that this leaf uses projection onto the intersection of an activated block; block Bregman projection can also denote sequential or parallel blockwise updates. The intended mathematical version is therefore source-dependent.

children.title: Projection Coverage Schedules
children.top_down_role: Deterministic or randomized schedules governing set or block coverage.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Coverage Schedules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fairness conditions ensuring scheduled projection methods repeatedly address every constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For blocks \(I_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), an infinite-coverage schedule satisfies \[\forall i\in\{1,\ldots,m\},\qquad \#\{k\geq0:i\in I_k\}=\infty.\] A bounded-coverage schedule satisfies the stronger condition that some integer \(T\geq1\) obeys \[\forall k\geq0,\qquad \bigcup_{s=k}^{k+T-1}I_s=\{1,\ldots,m\}.\] Bounded coverage implies infinite coverage and supplies a uniform maximum delay between consecutive visits to each constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fair schedule visits every constraint infinitely often; bounded coverage requires every constraint to appear within each fixed-length window.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bounded coverage implies infinite coverage for every constraint index.

notation.meaning: constraint block activated at iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two coverage conditions are precise and bounded coverage indeed implies infinite coverage, but this nontrivial schedule terminology has no cited source.

children.title: Bregman Proximal Methods
children.top_down_role: Generalized proximal constructions using non-Euclidean proximity.

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Proximal Point Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact proximal-point iteration using a general Bregman divergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:C\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, and let \(h\) generate a well-defined Bregman divergence on \(C\). Initialize \(x_0\in C\). Given \(\lambda_k>0\), compute \[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\left\{f(x)+\lambda_k^{-1}D_h(x,x_k)\right\}.\] Stop when a prescribed optimality residual, iterate-change criterion, or iteration limit is met, and return the current iterate. The Euclidean proximal point method is recovered from \(h(x)=\tfrac12\lVert x\rVert^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Bregman proximal point method repeatedly minimizes the full objective plus a Bregman distance from the current iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex on \(C\).
\(h\) is differentiable and strictly convex on the relevant domain.
Each proximal subproblem attains a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}\) is the Bregman proximal point of \(x_k\) for parameter \(\lambda_k\).

knowledge_statements.title: Entropic Proximal Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bregman proximal updates on the probability simplex using negative entropy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On the simplex \(\Delta_n=\{x\in\mathbb{R}_+^n:\sum_{i=1}^n x_i=1\}\), take \(h(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\log x_i\), with the convention \(0\log 0=0\). For \(y\in\operatorname{ri}(\Delta_n)\), the associated divergence is \(D_h(x,y)=\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\log(x_i/y_i)\). Given \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(\eta>0\), the entropic proximal update is \[x^+=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\Delta_n}\left\{\eta\langle g,x\rangle+D_h(x,y)\right\},\qquad x_i^+=\frac{y_i e^{-\eta g_i}}{\sum_{j=1}^n y_j e^{-\eta g_j}}.\] Applying this update to successive objective linearizations gives entropic mirror descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the simplex, the negative-entropy proximal update rescales coordinates multiplicatively and normalizes them; applying it to successive linearizations gives entropic mirror descent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^+\) is uniquely given by the normalized exponential update.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite Bregman Proximal Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mirror-proximal interface for a smooth-plus-nonsmooth composite objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(C\subseteq E\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(F=f+r\) on \(C\), where \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable and convex and \(r:C\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex. Let \(h:U\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable and strictly convex on an open convex set \(U\supseteq C\), with \(D_h(x,y)=h(x)-h(y)-\langle\nabla h(y),x-y\rangle\). Given \(x_k\in C\) and \(\eta_k>0\), compute \[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\left\{\langle\nabla f(x_k),x-x_k\rangle+r(x)+\eta_k^{-1}D_h(x,x_k)\right\}.\] Thus only \(f\) is linearized, while \(r\) remains inside the Bregman proximal subproblem. Stop using a prescribed composite optimality residual or iteration limit and return the selected iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The composite interface linearizes the smooth term while treating the nonsmooth term exactly inside a Bregman proximal update.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is finite-dimensional and \(C\subseteq E\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable and convex, and \(r:C\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(h:U\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable and strictly convex on an open convex set \(U\supseteq C\).
Each displayed Bregman proximal subproblem has a solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}\) is the composite Bregman proximal-gradient update at \(x_k\).

notation.meaning: Bregman divergence defining the proximal geometry

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Splitting Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resolvent interface for combining Bregman geometry with a split monotone inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space with dual \(E^*\), let \(A:Eightrightarrows E^*\) be an operator handled implicitly, and let \(B:E	o E^*\) be an operator handled explicitly. For the inclusion \(0\in A(x)+B(x)\), let \(h:U	o\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable and strictly convex on an open convex iterate domain \(U\subseteq E\). Given \(x_k\in U\) and \(\lambda_k>0\), choose \[x_{k+1}\in(
abla h+\lambda_k A)^{-1} igl(
abla h(x_k)-\lambda_k B(x_k) igr).\] Equivalently, \[0\in A(x_{k+1})+B(x_k)+\lambda_k^{-1} igl(
abla h(x_{k+1})-
abla h(x_k) igr).\] This specifies the geometric forward-backward interface; convergence additionally depends on monotonicity, regularity, and step-size conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bregman forward-backward splitting treats one operator implicitly and another explicitly in the dual coordinates induced by the kernel.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space, \(A:E\rightrightarrows E^*\), and \(B:E\to E^*\).
\(h:U\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable and strictly convex on an open convex iterate domain \(U\subseteq E\).
\(\lambda_k>0\), and the displayed inverse has at least one admissible value in \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inverse-image and inclusion formulas define the same Bregman forward-backward step.

knowledge_statements.title: ADMM Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bregman-proximal regularization attached to standard two-block ADMM subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\), \(Z\), and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, let \(A:X\to Y\) and \(B:Z\to Y\) be linear maps, and consider \[\min_{x\in X,\,z\in Z}\{f(x)+g(z):Ax+Bz=c\},\qquad c\in Y.\] Choose \(\rho>0\), differentiable strictly convex kernels \(\phi\) on \(X\) and \(\psi\) on \(Z\), and initialize \((x_0,z_0,u_0)\in X\times Z\times Y\). With \(D_\phi(x,y)=\phi(x)-\phi(y)-\langle\nabla\phi(y),x-y\rangle\) and analogously for \(D_\psi\), a proximal Bregman-ADMM interface is \[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax+Bz_k-c+u_k\rVert^2+D_\phi(x,x_k)\right\},\] \[z_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in Z}\left\{g(z)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax_{k+1}+Bz-c+u_k\rVert^2+D_\psi(z,z_k)\right\},\qquad u_{k+1}=u_k+Ax_{k+1}+Bz_{k+1}-c.\] Stop using prescribed primal and dual residual tolerances and return the current primal pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ADMM interface adds Bregman proximal terms to alternating primal subproblems while retaining the usual scaled-dual residual update.
assumptions_latex: \(X\), \(Z\), and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, and \(A:X\to Y\) and \(B:Z\to Y\) are linear.
\(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Z\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper, closed, and convex.
\(\phi\) and \(\psi\) are differentiable and strictly convex on domains containing the iterates.
The two displayed subproblems attain minimizers, and \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration is scaled two-block ADMM augmented by Bregman proximal regularization of both primal blocks.

notation.meaning: scaled dual iterate in the constraint space

children.title: Splitting Ownership Boundary
children.top_down_role: Scope separation between Bregman constructions and dedicated splitting or ADMM families.

knowledge_statements.title: Splitting Ownership Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes a single Bregman proximal step from operator-splitting and ADMM constructions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=f+g\) on a finite-dimensional space and let \(h\) generate \(D_h\). The update \[x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_x\left\{g(x)+\langle s^k,x\rangle+\frac{1}{\alpha_k}D_h(x,x^k)\right\},\qquad s^k\in\partial f(x^k),\] remains a Bregman proximal or mirror step because it solves one regularized primal subproblem. A construction crosses into splitting ownership when one iteration separately applies resolvents or proximal maps associated with distinct operators, or introduces blockwise primal updates and a multiplier update for a constraint such as \(Ax+Bz=c\). Replacing a quadratic penalty in ADMM by a Bregman distance does not remove this splitting structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A method belongs to splitting or ADMM once it separately resolves component operators or alternates constrained blocks and multipliers; merely using a Bregman penalty does not make it a single mirror step.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is differentiable and strictly convex on the iterates' domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{separate component resolvents or block-multiplier updates}\Longrightarrow\text{splitting ownership}.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Smoothness Descent Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies the relative-smoothness hypothesis that converts a Bregman model step into a descent method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For differentiable convex \(f\) and differentiable strictly convex \(h\) on a convex domain, relative \(L\)-smoothness means \[f(y)\le f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+L D_h(y,x)\] for all admissible \(x,y\). If \(g\) is convex and \(x^+\) minimizes \(g(y)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+\alpha^{-1}D_h(y,x)\), then \(\alpha\le L^{-1}\) gives \[f(x^+)+g(x^+)\le f(x)+g(x)-(\alpha^{-1}-L)D_h(x^+,x).\] Without the relative-smoothness inequality, the displayed Bregman model supplies no general descent guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Bregman proximal-gradient step is descending when the smooth term is relatively smooth with respect to the kernel and the step is at most the reciprocal relative-smoothness constant.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and convex, while \(g\) is proper convex.
\(h\) is differentiable and strictly convex on a convex domain.

notation.meaning: Bregman divergence of h from x to y

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The descent inequality is plausible and internally consistent, but no citation supports the exact relative-smoothness hypotheses or boundary claim.

children.title: Inertial Bregman Constructions
children.top_down_role: Bregman constructions incorporating trajectory-dependent inertial structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Inertial Bregman Constructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A basic extrapolate-then-Bregman-proximal inertial template for convex composite minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x^{-1}=x^0\), steps \(\alpha_k>0\), inertial parameters \(0\le\beta_k<1\), and \(F=f+g\), form \[y^k=x^k+\beta_k(x^k-x^{k-1}),\qquad x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_x\left\{g(x)+\langle v^k,x-y^k\rangle+\frac{1}{\alpha_k}D_h(x,y^k)\right\},\] where \(v^k\in\partial f(y^k)\), or \(v^k=\nabla f(y^k)\) in the differentiable case. The parameters must ensure that \(y^k\) lies in the Bregman kernel's differentiability domain. Stop by a prescribed iteration limit or residual test and return the last iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inertial template extrapolates from the two latest iterates, then performs a Bregman-regularized subgradient or gradient step at the extrapolated point.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is differentiable and strictly convex wherever \(y^k\) and \(x^{k+1}\) lie.
Each displayed subproblem has a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}\) is the Bregman proximal response to the extrapolated point \(y^k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the construction leaf, but the particular extrapolate-then-Bregman-subgradient template and its admissible-domain conditions require a source.

children.title: Accelerated Bregman Constructions
children.top_down_role: Bregman constructions organized around accelerated estimate or coupling frameworks.

knowledge_statements.title: Accelerated Bregman Constructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accelerated composite Bregman rate under relative smoothness and quadratic triangle scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=f+g\) be convex, let \(f\) be differentiable and relatively \(L\)-smooth with respect to \(h\), and suppose the accelerated Bregman construction uses estimate-sequence weights \(A_k\) satisfying \(A_k\ge (k+1)^2/(4L)\). If its estimate-sequence invariant is \[A_kF(x^k)\le A_kF(x^\star)+D_h(x^\star,x^0),\] then \[F(x^k)-F(x^\star)\le\frac{D_h(x^\star,x^0)}{A_k}\le\frac{4L D_h(x^\star,x^0)}{(k+1)^2}.\] Thus the accelerated construction reaches objective error at most \(\varepsilon\) in \(O(\sqrt{L D_h(x^\star,x^0)/\varepsilon})\) first-order iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An accelerated Bregman estimate-sequence method achieves an inverse-square objective rate when relative smoothness and the required quadratic Bregman geometry support quadratically growing weights.
assumptions_latex: \(F=f+g\) is convex and attains its minimum at \(x^\star\).
The construction satisfies the displayed estimate-sequence invariant and weight growth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x^k)-F(x^\star)\le 4L D_h(x^\star,x^0)/(k+1)^2.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed rate follows conditionally from the asserted invariant and weight growth, but no source establishes an accelerated construction satisfying them under the stated geometry. The record also presents only a complexity certificate in a construction container.

children.title: Acceleration Ownership Boundary
children.top_down_role: Separation from dedicated inertial, accelerated, or relative-smoothness method families.

knowledge_statements.title: Acceleration Ownership Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates inertial extrapolation from acceleration certified by an improved worst-case rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a Bregman method augmented by extrapolation \(y^k=x^k+\beta_k(x^k-x^{k-1})\). The extrapolation is inertial, but it is not by itself an acceleration certificate. Acceleration ownership requires a theorem showing a strictly improved worst-case complexity over the corresponding nonaccelerated method under the same objective and oracle class, for example \[F(x^k)-F^\star=O(k^{-2})\quad\text{instead of}\quad O(k^{-1})\] for convex relatively smooth composite minimization. If only asymptotic convergence, empirical speedup, or unchanged \(O(k^{-1})\) complexity is known, the construction remains inertial rather than rate-accelerated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Momentum is not automatically acceleration. Ownership requires a proved worst-case rate improvement under the same problem and oracle assumptions; empirical speedup or unchanged order is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: The inertial and reference methods are compared on the same problem class.
Both rates use the same first-order oracle and accuracy criterion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{inertial extrapolation alone}\not\Longrightarrow\text{certified acceleration}.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but the proposed ownership criterion and example rate comparison need an authoritative source defining acceleration for the same problem and oracle class.

children.title: Subgradient Convergence Family
children.top_down_role: Convergence routes distinguished by stepsize, output selection, and curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Diminishing-Stepsize Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected subgradient convergence with nonsummable but square-summable steps in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(f:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex with \(C\subset\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(X^\star=\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\ne\varnothing\). For \[x^{k+1}=P_C(x^k-\alpha_k g^k),\qquad g^k\in\partial f(x^k),\] assume \(\|g^k\|\le G\), \(\alpha_k>0\), \(\sum_{k=0}^\infty\alpha_k=\infty\), and \(\sum_{k=0}^\infty\alpha_k^2<\infty\). Then \[\min_{0\le i<k}f(x^i)\longrightarrow f^\star:=\min_{x\in C}f(x).\] The iterates are quasi-Fejér with respect to \(X^\star\), and every cluster point whose corresponding objective values converge to \(f^\star\) belongs to \(X^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper closed convex objective, bounded subgradients and positive nonsummable but square-summable steps make the projected-subgradient best values converge to the optimum. The iterates are quasi-Fejér relative to the solution set, and cluster points attained along objective-convergent subsequences are optimal.

\(f\) is proper, closed, and convex, \(C\subset\operatorname{dom}f\), and \(X^\star\ne\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.title: Constant-Stepsize Accuracy Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon and asymptotic error-floor bounds for projected subgradient descent with a fixed step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under projected subgradient descent on a closed convex set, suppose \(\|g^k\|\le G\), choose a constant step \(\alpha>0\), and let \(R=\|x^0-x^\star\|\) for a minimizer \(x^\star\). For every \(K\ge1\), \[\min_{0\le k<K}\bigl(f(x^k)-f^\star\bigr)\le\frac{R^2}{2\alpha K}+\frac{\alpha G^2}{2}.\] Consequently, \[\liminf_{k\to\infty}f(x^k)\le f^\star+\frac{\alpha G^2}{2}.\] A fixed nonzero step therefore generally guarantees approach only to an \(O(\alpha G^2)\) objective neighborhood, not exact convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed subgradient step gives a transient term decreasing as one over the horizon plus an error floor proportional to the step and squared subgradient bound.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex on a nonempty closed convex set and has a minimizer \(x^\star\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{0\le k<K}(f(x^k)-f^\star)\le R^2/(2\alpha K)+\alpha G^2/2.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Ergodic Subgradient Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted-average objective guarantee for projected subgradient descent with arbitrary positive steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let convex \(f\) attain its minimum over \(C\) at \(x^\star\), and define \(R=\|x^0-x^\star\|\). For an integer \(K\ge1\), let \[x^{k+1}=P_C(x^k-\alpha_k g^k),\qquad g^k\in\partial f(x^k),\qquad \|g^k\|\le G,\qquad \alpha_k>0,\] for \(0\le k<K\), and define \[\bar x^K=\frac{\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\alpha_kx^k}{\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\alpha_k}.\] Then \[f(\bar x^K)-f^\star\le\frac{R^2+G^2\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\alpha_k^2}{2\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\alpha_k}.\] If \(G>0\) and the prescribed-horizon choice is \(\alpha_k=R/(G\sqrt K)\), then \(f(\bar x^K)-f^\star\le RG/\sqrt K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every positive iteration horizon, the stepsize-weighted average satisfies an explicit objective bound. Defining R as the initial distance to a minimizer, a horizon-tuned constant step gives the standard inverse-square-root rate.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and convex \(f\) has a minimizer \(x^\star\) over \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\bar x^K)-f^\star\le(R^2+G^2\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\alpha_k^2)/(2\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\alpha_k)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best-objective-value guarantee for projected subgradient descent with arbitrary positive steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let convex \(f\) attain its minimum over \(C\) at \(x^\star\). For an integer \(K\ge1\), let \[x^{k+1}=P_C(x^k-\alpha_k g^k),\qquad g^k\in\partial f(x^k),\qquad \|g^k\|\le G,\qquad \alpha_k>0,\] for \(0\le k<K\), and select \(i_K\in\arg\min_{0\le k<K}f(x^k)\). Then \[f(x^{i_K})-f^\star\le\frac{\|x^0-x^\star\|^2+G^2\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\alpha_k^2}{2\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\alpha_k}.\] If \(G>0\), \(R\ge\|x^0-x^\star\|\), and \(\alpha_k=R/(G\sqrt K)\) for the prescribed horizon, then \(f(x^{i_K})-f^\star\le RG/\sqrt K\).

knowledge_statements.title: Ergodic–Best-Iterate Comparison
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that ergodic and best-iterate objective values admit no universal ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For positive weights \(w_i\), convexity gives \[f\!\left(\frac{\sum_iw_ix_i}{\sum_iw_i}\right)\le\frac{\sum_iw_if(x_i)}{\sum_iw_i},\qquad \min_i f(x_i)\le\frac{\sum_iw_if(x_i)}{\sum_iw_i},\] but neither candidate universally dominates the other. With equal weights, \(f(x)=|x|\), and \((x_1,x_2)=(-1,1)\), the average has value \(0\) while the best iterate has value \(1\). With \(f(x)=e^x\) and \((x_1,x_2)=(0,2)\), the average has value \(e\), while the best iterate has value \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Both outputs are bounded by the weighted mean of iterate values, but either can be better: averaging helps absolute value across symmetric points, while the best iterate wins for an exponential example.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex on a convex domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\bar x)\) and \(\min_i f(x_i)\) have no universal ordering over convex objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Convex Subgradient Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse-linear objective rate for weighted averaging under strong convexity and bounded subgradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex on a closed convex set \(C\), let \(\|g^k\|\le G\), and run \[x^{k+1}=P_C(x^k-\alpha_k g^k),\qquad \alpha_k=\frac{2}{\mu(k+2)}.\] For the linearly weighted average \[\bar x^K=\frac{2}{K(K+1)}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}(k+1)x^k,\] the standard strongly convex projected-subgradient analysis yields \[f(\bar x^K)-f^\star\le\frac{2G^2}{\mu(K+1)}.\] Hence an objective error at most \(\varepsilon\) requires \(O(G^2/(\mu\varepsilon))\) subgradient-oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity improves the weighted averaged subgradient rate from inverse square root to inverse linear, giving oracle complexity proportional to the squared Lipschitz bound over strong convexity and accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, \(\mu\)-strongly convex on nonempty closed convex \(C\), and attains its minimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyak-Stepsize Convergence Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected subgradient convergence using the known optimal value in the Polyak stepsize.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(f:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex with \(C\subset\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(X^\star=\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\ne\varnothing\). Suppose the optimal value \(f^\star\) is known. If \(f(x^k)=f^\star\), stop. Otherwise choose \(g^k\in\partial f(x^k)\) with \(0<\|g^k\|\le G\) and set \[\alpha_k=\frac{f(x^k)-f^\star}{\|g^k\|^2},\qquad x^{k+1}=P_C(x^k-\alpha_k g^k).\] Then every \(x^\star\in X^\star\) satisfies \[\|x^{k+1}-x^\star\|^2\le\|x^k-x^\star\|^2-\frac{(f(x^k)-f^\star)^2}{\|g^k\|^2}.\] Unless the method stops finitely at a minimizer, \(f(x^k)\to f^\star\), and every cluster point of the iterates belongs to \(X^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the optimal value is known, the method stops upon reaching it; otherwise the Polyak step produces Fejér decrease proportional to squared objective error. For a proper closed convex objective and bounded nonzero selected subgradients, objective values converge to the optimum and all cluster points are optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(f\) is proper, closed, and convex, \(C\subset\operatorname{dom}f\), and \(X^\star\ne\varnothing\).
At every nonoptimal iterate, \(g^k\in\partial f(x^k)\) and \(0<\|g^k\|\le G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x^k)\to f^\star\) unless finite termination occurs, and every cluster point belongs to \(X^\star\).

knowledge_statements.title: Sharpness-Driven Subgradient Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyak-step rate under global weak sharpness and bounded subgradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be convex on a closed convex set \(C\), with nonempty solution set \(X^*\) and value \(f^*\). Assume \(f(x)-f^*\ge \mu\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\) and \(\|g\|_*\le G\) for every \(x\in C\) and \(g\in\partial f(x)\), where \(0<\mu\le G\). For \(g_k\ne0\), set \(\alpha_k=(f(x_k)-f^*)/\|g_k\|_*^2\) and \(x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-\alpha_k g_k)\) in Euclidean geometry. Then
\[\operatorname{dist}(x_{k+1},X^*)^2\le\left(1-\frac{\mu^2}{G^2}\right)\operatorname{dist}(x_k,X^*)^2.\]
Thus squared distance decreases geometrically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under global sharpness, bounded subgradients, and known optimum value, Polyak subgradient steps contract squared distance to the solution set by a fixed factor.
assumptions_latex: \(f^*\) is known and Euclidean projection onto \(C\) is available
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,X^*)^2\le(1-\mu^2/G^2)^k\operatorname{dist}(x_0,X^*)^2\)

notation.meaning: set of minimizers of f over C

knowledge_statements.title: Offline Mirror-Descent Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic weighted-average guarantee for constrained convex minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be closed and convex, let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be convex, and let \(h\) be differentiable and \(1\)-strongly convex with Bregman divergence \(D_h\). Given \(x_1\in C\), steps \(\eta_t>0\), and \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\), define
\[x_{t+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in C}\left\{\eta_t\langle g_t,x\rangle+D_h(x,x_t)\right\},\qquad \bar x_T=\frac{\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t x_t}{\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t}.\]
For every minimizer \(x^*\),
\[f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\le\frac{D_h(x^*,x_1)+\tfrac12\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t^2\|g_t\|_*^2}{\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deterministic mirror descent bounds the weighted-average objective error by initial Bregman distance plus accumulated squared step-gradient terms, divided by total step length.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and attains its minimum on \(C\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\bar x_T)-f^*\le[D_h(x^*,x_1)+\tfrac12\sum_t\eta_t^2\|g_t\|_*^2]/\sum_t\eta_t\)

knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Convex Mirror-Descent Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted mirror-descent rate under relative strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h\) be differentiable and \(1\)-strongly convex on \(C\). Suppose \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex relative to \(h\): for every \(x,y\in C\) and \(g\in\partial f(x)\),
\[f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle+\mu D_h(y,x).\]
Assume \(\|g_t\|_*\le G\). Run mirror descent with \(\eta_t=2/[\mu(t+1)]\), and form \(\widetilde x_T=2\sum_{t=1}^T t x_t/[T(T+1)]\). Then
\[f(\widetilde x_T)-f^*\le\frac{2G^2}{\mu(T+1)}.\]
Consequently, \(T=O(G^2/(\mu\varepsilon))\) iterations suffice for objective error at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative strong convexity improves weighted mirror descent from the general square-root rate to an inverse-linear objective rate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\widetilde x_T)-f^*\le2G^2/[\mu(T+1)]\)

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Mirror-Descent Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected weighted-average guarantee with unbiased stochastic subgradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=\mathbb E[F(x,\xi)]\) be convex on \(C\), and let \(h\) be differentiable and \(1\)-strongly convex. With filtration \((\mathcal F_t)\), suppose the oracle returns \(G_t\) satisfying \(\mathbb E[G_t\mid\mathcal F_t]\in\partial f(x_t)\) and \(\mathbb E[\|G_t\|_*^2\mid\mathcal F_t]\le G^2\). Define
\[x_{t+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in C}\{\eta_t\langle G_t,x\rangle+D_h(x,x_t)\},\qquad \bar x_T=\frac{\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t x_t}{\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t}.\]
Then
\[\mathbb E[f(\bar x_T)]-f^*\le\frac{D_h(x^*,x_1)+\tfrac12G^2\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t^2}{\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With conditionally unbiased, bounded-second-moment oracle outputs, stochastic mirror descent satisfies the deterministic mirror bound in expectation.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x)=\mathbb E[F(x,\xi)]\) is convex and has a minimizer
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[f(\bar x_T)]-f^*\le[D_h(x^*,x_1)+\tfrac12G^2\sum_t\eta_t^2]/\sum_t\eta_t\)

knowledge_statements.title: Online Mirror-Descent Regret
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static-regret bound for online mirror descent with convex losses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be convex, let each \(\ell_t:C\to\mathbb R\) be convex, and choose \(g_t\in\partial\ell_t(x_t)\). If \(h\) is differentiable and \(1\)-strongly convex, online mirror descent sets
\[x_{t+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in C}\{\eta_t\langle g_t,x\rangle+D_h(x,x_t)\}.\]
For nonincreasing \(\eta_t>0\) and every comparator \(u\in C\),
\[\sum_{t=1}^T(\ell_t(x_t)-\ell_t(u))\le\frac{D_h(u,x_1)}{\eta_T}+\frac12\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t\|g_t\|_*^2.\]
If \(D_h(u,x_1)\le R^2\), \(\|g_t\|_*\le G\), and \(\eta_t=R/(G\sqrt t)\), the regret is \(O(RG\sqrt T)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Online mirror descent controls regret by comparator Bregman distance and accumulated squared dual-gradient norms, yielding square-root regret with bounded geometry and gradients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Reg}_T(u)\le D_h(u,x_1)/\eta_T+\tfrac12\sum_t\eta_t\|g_t\|_*^2\)

knowledge_statements.title: Online-to-Batch Mirror Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected-risk conversion for i.i.d. convex losses and averaged online iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_T\) be i.i.d., let \(\ell(\cdot;Z)\) be convex on \(C\), and define \(f(x)=\mathbb E[\ell(x;Z)]\). Suppose each \(x_t\) is measurable with respect to \(Z_1,
\ldots,Z_{t-1}\). For weights \(w_t>0\), set \(W_T=\sum_{t=1}^T w_t\) and \(\bar x_T=W_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T w_t x_t\). Then every \(u\in C\) satisfies
\[\mathbb E[f(\bar x_T)]-f(u)\le\frac{1}{W_T}\mathbb E\left[\sum_{t=1}^T w_t\bigl(\ell(x_t;Z_t)-\ell(u;Z_t)\bigr)\right].\]
Thus a weighted regret bound for online mirror descent becomes an expected excess-risk bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For i.i.d. convex losses, averaging predictable online iterates converts weighted expected regret into expected excess population risk.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[f(\bar x_T)]-f(u)\le W_T^{-1}\mathbb E[\sum_t w_t(\ell(x_t;Z_t)-\ell(u;Z_t))]\)

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Averaging Offline Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Offline convergence obtained from regularized dual-averaging regret.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be convex, and let \(h:C\to[0,\infty)\) be \(1\)-strongly convex with \(\min_C h=0\). For \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\) and nondecreasing \(\beta_t>0\), define \(s_t=\sum_{i=1}^t g_i\) and
\[x_{t+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in C}\{\langle s_t,x\rangle+\beta_{t+1}h(x)\}.\]
With \(\bar x_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\), every minimizer \(x^*\) satisfies
\[f(\bar x_T)-f^*\le\frac{\beta_{T+1}h(x^*)+\tfrac12\sum_{t=1}^T\|g_t\|_*^2/\beta_t}{T}.\]
Appropriate \(\beta_t\) proportional to \(\sqrt t\) yields an \(O(T^{-1/2})\) rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularized dual averaging converts cumulative linearized-loss control into an offline objective bound for the average iterate, with a square-root rate under bounded subgradients.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and attains its minimum on \(C\)
\(h\ge0\) is \(1\)-strongly convex and has minimum zero
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\bar x_T)-f^*\le[\beta_{T+1}h(x^*)+\tfrac12\sum_t\|g_t\|_*^2/\beta_t]/T\)

notation.meaning: sum of observed subgradients through iteration t

Exact indexing and constants require a dual-averaging source.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite Dual-Averaging Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularized dual averaging for a smooth-or-nonsmooth loss plus simple convex penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=f(x)+\psi(x)\) on \(C\), where \(f\) and \(\psi\) are proper convex functions and the proximal subproblem involving \(\psi\) is solvable. Let \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\), \(s_t=\sum_{i=1}^t g_i\), and let \(h\ge0\) be \(1\)-strongly convex. Composite dual averaging uses
\[x_{t+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in C}\{\langle s_t,x\rangle+t\psi(x)+\beta_{t+1}h(x)\}.\]
For nondecreasing \(\beta_t>0\), its average \(\bar x_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\) satisfies
\[F(\bar x_T)-F(x^*)\le\frac{\beta_{T+1}h(x^*)+\tfrac12\sum_{t=1}^T\|g_t\|_*^2/\beta_t}{T}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composite dual averaging accumulates subgradients of one term while retaining the simple penalty exactly, and its average obeys the usual dual-averaging error bound.
assumptions_latex: The displayed composite proximal subproblem has a minimizer
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(\bar x_T)-F(x^*)\le[\beta_{T+1}h(x^*)+\tfrac12\sum_t\|g_t\|_*^2/\beta_t]/T\)

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Dual-Averaging Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Saddle-gap guarantee obtained from dual-averaging regret on both variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be convex and let \(L:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\) be convex in \(x\) and concave in \(y\). Suppose primal and dual regularized dual-averaging procedures generate \(x_t,y_t\) and have regrets \(R_T^x(x)\) against losses \(L(\cdot,y_t)\) and \(R_T^y(y)\) against losses \(-L(x_t,\cdot)\). For \(\bar x_T=T^{-1}\sum_t x_t\) and \(\bar y_T=T^{-1}\sum_t y_t\),
\[L(\bar x_T,y)-L(x,\bar y_T)\le\frac{R_T^x(x)+R_T^y(y)}{T}\qquad(x\in X,\ y\in Y).\]
Hence sublinear regret on both sides yields a vanishing primal–dual saddle gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Running dual averaging on both sides of a convex-concave game bounds the averaged saddle gap by the sum of the two players’ regrets divided by time.
assumptions_latex: Both dual-averaging regret bounds hold against fixed comparators
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{y\in Y}L(\bar x_T,y)-\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\bar y_T)\le[\sup_x R_T^x(x)+\sup_y R_T^y(y)]/T\)
review_flags: Supplied primal-dual sources do not explicitly identify this dual-averaging guarantee.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A complexity bound is an appropriate role for this primal-dual guarantee, and the pointwise regret-to-saddle-gap relation is plausible. The precise sign conventions and definitions of the two regrets are not given, and no source locator identifies this dual-averaging result; the supremum-form conclusion therefore requires sourced verification.

knowledge_statements.title: Online Dual-Averaging Regret Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Square-root minimax boundary and failure without bounded gradients or comparator geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On a convex decision set \(C\), regularized dual averaging with a \(1\)-strongly convex regularizer satisfies, for every comparator \(u\),
\[\operatorname{Reg}_T(u)\le \beta_{T+1}h(u)+\frac12\sum_{t=1}^T\frac{\|g_t\|_*^2}{\beta_t}.\]
If \(h(u)\le R^2\), \(\|g_t\|_*\le G\), and \(\beta_t\) is chosen on the scale \(G\sqrt t/R\), this is \(O(RG\sqrt T)\), matching the worst-case order for online linear optimization. If either comparator regularizer radius or gradient norms are unrestricted, the displayed control need not be sublinear; adversarial linear losses can produce regret proportional to \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual averaging achieves the optimal square-root regret order only with bounded comparator geometry and gradients; removing these controls permits linear adversarial regret.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Reg}_T=O(RG\sqrt T)\) under boundedness, while unrestricted instances may have \(\operatorname{Reg}_T=\Omega(T)\)
review_flags: No supplied source covers both the dual-averaging upper bound and matching online lower boundary.
The linear-regret failure mechanism requires a precise adversarial model locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind is appropriate for this terminal container. However, no source supports both the dual-averaging upper bound and the asserted matching minimax and linear-regret boundaries. The adversary, comparator class, loss scaling, and meaning of removing each boundedness condition must be fixed by a precise locator.

children.title: Nonsmooth Oracle Complexity
children.top_down_role: Upper and lower oracle-complexity families, including geometry and finite-dimensional effects.

knowledge_statements.title: General Nonsmooth Upper Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Black-box upper complexity for Lipschitz convex minimization over bounded domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be convex on a closed convex subset of a Euclidean space. Assume a minimizer \(x^*\) exists, \(\|x_1-x^*\|\le R\), and every oracle subgradient used by the method has norm at most \(G\). Projected subgradient descent with constant step \(\eta=R/(G\sqrt T)\) and average \(\bar x_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\) satisfies
\[f(\bar x_T)-f^*\le\frac{RG}{\sqrt T}.\]
Therefore at most
\[T=\left\lceil\frac{R^2G^2}{\varepsilon^2}\right\rceil\]
first-order oracle calls suffice to obtain objective error at most \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected subgradient method solves bounded-domain Lipschitz convex minimization to objective accuracy epsilon using on the order of the inverse squared accuracy oracle calls.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and attains its minimum on \(C\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T=O(R^2G^2/\varepsilon^2)\) first-order oracle calls suffice

notation.meaning: initial distance bound to a minimizer
